title: argon2id — case shape (v0.1)
description: Pins protocol::derive_password_wrap_key + protocol::derive_recovery_wrap_key_from_normalized byte mapping under canonical Phase 1 Argon2id parameters (m_kib=262144 = 256 MiB, t=3, p=2, argon2_version=0x13). Single case_kind (round-trip pin only); the input_path field dispatches password-side vs recovery-side at the runner level. EXPECTED RUNTIME: ~3 seconds per case at canonical params; 6 cases → ~18 seconds added to `cargo test`. Default-on (NOT #[ignore]-gated) — protocol-contract assertion warrants default execution. Spec contract: docs/spec/protocol.md §3 (KDF + salt prefixes) + §4 (KDF parameter block) + decisions.md 2026-04-26 KDF-calibration entry.

vector_id.description: Stable identifier of the form 'argon2id/v0.1/<descriptive-slug>'. Immutable once shipped.

input_path.description: Which derivation path to exercise. 'password' → derive_password_wrap_key (raw user input, NOT normalized — passwords are not BIP-39 phrases). 'recovery' → derive_recovery_wrap_key_from_normalized (input MUST already be NFKD-normalized per spec §3.4).

input_password_or_phrase_utf8_hex.description: UTF-8 byte encoding of the password (path=password) or NFKD-normalized phrase (path=recovery). Hex-encoded for cross-language portability.

input_salt_random_hex.description: 16-byte Argon2id salt entropy. Combined with account_number_hash + the path-specific salt prefix to produce the canonical salt fed into Argon2id.

input_account_number_hash_hex.description: 16-byte SHA-256-truncated account-number hash. Bound into the salt construction per spec §3.1 to prevent precomputation across accounts.

m_kib.description: v0.1 canonical: 256 MiB. Future v0.1.x variants in mobile profile may differ — vectors carry the field for explicit pinning.

input_kdf_params.description: Canonical Phase 1 Argon2id parameter block. All 4 fields pinned to const values in v0.1; relaxed in v005.

expected_wrap_key_hex.description: 32-byte derived wrap-key output. Implementations call the matching derive_* function and compare byte-equal.
